context: Cycle plot of U.S. monthly retail sales 2020–2024: 12 panels (one per month), each showing 5 yearly data points connected by a trend line, with a dashed per-month mean line and a shared Y-axis.
first_impression: A structurally honest cycle plot with data-driven domains, appropriate non-zero baseline for a dot/line chart, and clear year-color encoding.
what_works: Y-axis domain is fully data-driven via d3.min/d3.max (no hardcoded magic numbers), and the truncated baseline (~$60) is correct for a line/dot chart focused on variance rather than magnitude from zero; per-month mean lines add honest reference without distortion.
what_doesnt: No key function in .data(monthData) joins (minor robustness gap if updates were ever added), and the line generator has no .defined() guard — safe here because synthetic data is complete, but would silently draw false continuity over any real missing values.
